en: Using an inclined plane like a ramp lets you push heavy boxes safely without straining your back muscles.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the floor, preventing dangerous slips and falls on wet surfaces.
Wearing a helmet protects your head from injury when gravity pulls you down during a bicycle fall.
Keep strong neodymium magnets away from electronic devices because their magnetic fields can permanently erase stored digital data.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because water is a conductor that can transmit dangerous electrical shocks.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light rays from damaging the sensitive cells inside your eyes.
Wearing foam earplugs at loud events reduces sound energy entering your ears, preventing permanent hearing damage.
Using thick cloth oven mitts acts as a thermal insulator, preventing heat from burning your hands on hot pans.
Eating carbohydrate-rich foods like rice provides your body with chemical energy required for daily physical activities and muscle movement.
Plugging too many appliances into a single extension cord overheats the wires, creating a serious electrical fire hazard.
Rubbing your cold hands together converts mechanical energy into thermal energy, generating heat to warm your skin.
Using a wheelbarrow combines a lever and wheel-and-axle to move heavy soil without straining your arm muscles.
